<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/runtime/config (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via /api/settings/deployment/notice (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-map.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/runtime/config (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/runtime/config (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6a34e84aec0a88ac3ea558f4541e07848680e566` — the merge of head `f1521e974a71b3b0cd45fdc05c19d99c85d7adea` into base `7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6a34e84aec0a88ac3ea558f4541e07848680e566 && git checkout 6a34e84aec0a88ac3ea558f4541e07848680e566
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 f1521e974a71b3b0cd45fdc05c19d99c85d7adea && git checkout -B drift-repro 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 && git merge --no-ff f1521e974a71b3b0cd45fdc05c19d99c85d7adea

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f1521e974a71b3b0cd45fdc05c19d99c85d7adea`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is on the changeset and the PR body. There is no published schema in the diff and no governed path (`check-governed-merges --pr 34240`: NOT governed). Inputs read: cards #34186, #34187 and #34188, triage's first-touch comments, and the claims of 00:22Z; the os-dev-reports 6905347991, 6905359085 and 6905365224; the PR #34240 body; the net diff against `main` at the merge base (16 files); and the check-runs on this head (2026-11-16T02:35Z: 49 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 0 failed).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The widening.** One new key, `features.deploymentNotice: boolean`, on `GET /api/v1/runtime/config`. The name is the seat's ruling. The console's `RuntimeFeatures` mirror gains the same member. Nothing is removed or renamed. `features` is not declared in a spec schema (checked: `packages/spec` has no `installLocal` / runtime-config `features` shape). Right.
- **Observed, not declared.** `SettingsServicePlugin` registers the door as the kernel service `settings.deployment-notice` exactly when it mounts the routes with it. `RuntimeConfigPlugin` reads that registration per request, and writes the key after the host's `...features`, so a `resolveFeatures` policy can neither claim a notice the host does not serve nor withhold one it does. A host that mounts the settings routes itself registers nothing and reports `false`. The route table cannot tell the two arms apart, so the service registration is the right source. The spelled-out service name in cloud-connection (no package dependency) is pinned by a test that mounts the real settings plugin. Right.
- **Back-compat.** The console reads an absent key as `true` (`!== false`), so a self-hosted runtime older than the key keeps its notice. Only an explicit `false` stops the read. Right.
- **#34187.** The catalog's side load asks `listLocalInstalls()` only when `features.installLocal` is true, the package page's existing gate. The other two reads are unchanged. Right.
- **#34188.** In the names-only arm, lookup targets not already asked are first probed in one `GET /meta/object?names=` read (the #29444 batch hand-off), and only served targets are read by name. The package arm is unchanged. The dev measured that the card's premise ("the package arm already batch-reads") does not hold for off-package targets. That class remainder, plus the same read for `requiresObject`, is filed as #34244. `Fixes #34188` stands: the card's measured case (the control plane's Members page, packageless) is fixed and pinned.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`.** No authoring key is added or removed. Right.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` and `@object-ui/app-shell`. Under AGENTS.md's changeset rule a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- File surface: within the claims. Five harnesses were edited as declared forced edits, named in the PR body.
- Open questions, ruled: (1) package-arm targets → #34244; (2) a bundle-held target costs one batch read per name set → accepted, revisit only on a measured cold-load regression; (3) `requiresObject` → folded into #34244.
- `security_findings`: none.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-5try4s`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmT2NE3iyG1o6TDg3sf`

**VERDICT: PASS**
